claim_text: Server-side sessions use opaque 256-bit session IDs stored in memory.
Password hashing uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations.
HttpOnly session cookies prevent XSS from accessing session tokens.
Session cookies use SameSite=Lax to prevent CSRF and allow external navigation.
Secure cookie flag is configurable via K9B_SECURE_COOKIE=true environment variable.
notes: Verified by TestSecureCookieConfig tests in ACT 2.7

claim_text: Session expiry defaults to 8 hours max age with 30 minute idle timeout.
All routes except auth endpoints require authentication.
Login errors do not disclose which field (username/password) failed.
Logout invalidates the server-side session.

Frontend TypeScript coverage enforces 90% line/statement coverage via Vitest threshold configuration.
Branch and function coverage are tracked but not enforced (informational only).

claim_text: AlertmanagerSourceRegistry (alertmanager-source-registry.json) is the authoritative cross-run source of truth for operator decisions.
Per-run override artifacts are NOT authoritative; they are derived support artifacts for UI display.

Each action creates a new artifact with unique artifactid (UUID); they survive beyond run-scoped overrides.
Every claim in the incident report is classified into one of five types: observed, derived, hypothesis, unknown, recommendation.
Observed claims never contain root-cause language (caused by, root cause, because of).
Hypothesis claims must have non-empty basis to use root-cause language.
Unknown claims must have whyMissing explanation and must NOT be omitted or invented.
The incident report and worklist are derived projections, not source-of-truth artifacts.
The agent never mutates live clusters autonomously; all adaptations pass through check-proposal replay validation and explicit operator approval.
k9b treats LLM output as advisory and reviewable, never as automatic truth.

The system never collapses observed signal, derived symptom, hypothesis, confidence, and recommended action into one opaque conclusion.
